concept.title: COMPRESSION_CODEC Query Option ( or higher only)

conbody.p: COMPRESSION_CODEC query option When Impala writes Parquet data files using the INSERT statement, the underlying compression is controlled by the COMPRESSION_CODEC query option.
conbody.note: Prior to Impala 2.0, this option was named PARQUET_COMPRESSION_CODEC. In Impala 2.0 and later, the PARQUET_COMPRESSION_CODEC name is not recognized. Use the more general name COMPRESSION_CODEC for new code.
conbody.codeblock: SET COMPRESSION_CODEC=codec_name; // Supported for all codecs. SET COMPRESSION_CODEC=codec_name:compression_level; // Only supported for ZSTD, GZIP and LZ4.
conbody.p: The allowed values for this query option are SNAPPY (the default), GZIP, ZSTD, LZ4, and NONE.

ZSTD, GZIP and LZ4 also support setting a compression level by appending :level to the codec name. For all of them, a lower level is faster but gives a lower compression ratio. A level outside the supported range, or a level for a codec that does not support levels, is rejected with an error. If no level is specified, the default level of the codec is used.

row.entry: From the minimum level of the ZSTD library (a large negative number, where negative levels trade compression ratio for speed) up to 22.
1, which uses the fast LZ4 compression, or 3 to 12, which use the LZ4 high compression (HC) mode. Level 2 and levels above 12 are not valid.

conbody.note: LZ4 high compression levels give a better compression ratio than level 1 at the cost of a longer write time, while keeping the fast decompression speed of LZ4. They are useful for data that is written once and read many times. The compression level only affects writing. Data files compressed at any level are read the same way.

A Parquet file created with COMPRESSION_CODEC=NONE is still typically smaller than the original data, due to encoding schemes such as run-length encoding and dictionary encoding that are applied separately from compression.
conbody.p: The option value is not case-sensitive.

If the option is set to an unrecognized value, all kinds of queries will fail due to the invalid option setting, not just queries involving Parquet tables. (The value BZIP2 is also recognized, but is not compatible with Parquet tables.)
